title: Customer incident orchestration playlet and concise status templates
body:
Purpose and audience:
This playlet collects compact, customer-focused communication artifacts for incidents that affect inference correctness, latency, or availability. Designed for Customer Success (CS), Incident Leads, and on-call operators who need rapid text to post to status.redwood.ai and to send targeted customer updates. The tone is plain, accountable, and focused on customer impact, options, and evidence they can use for reconciliation.

Goals: 
- Reduce time-to-first-public-update to under 15 minutes by providing pre-written, fillable snippets.
- Give customers clear, actionable choices (rollback, replay, safe-mode) and the evidence they need to decide.
- Keep postmortem language short, non-technical for executives, and attach a technical appendix for engineering/partners.

Structure of this draft playlet: 
1) Statuspage micro-updates (timeline-friendly snippets)
2) Customer-facing postmortem executive summary (single-paragraph + impact bullets)
3) Customer action card (choices & steps)
4) Evidence bundle checklist customers can request
5) Internal operator rehearsal checklist and unresolved questions to surface in reviews

1) Statuspage micro-updates (copy-and-paste ready)
- Initial preliminary: 
  Title: Degraded inference responses in US region (partial) – investigating
  Body: We are investigating reports of slow or inconsistent inference responses for some customers in the US region. Impact: intermittent elevated latency and occasional truncated/duplicate responses for a subset of requests. Scope: a small fraction of requests routed through the v2 serving tier. Mitigation: routing rollouts in progress; customers on Dedicated not impacted unless pinned to v2. We will post updates here every 30 minutes.

- Progress update (after mitigation step applied): 
  Title: Routing mitigation applied — monitoring
  Body: We have applied a routing mitigation to shift traffic away from the affected pool and are monitoring. Early indicators show lower latency and fewer truncated responses. If you still see issues, reply to your support thread with request ids and examples.

- Recovery notice: 
  Title: Service returned to expected behavior — validation ongoing
  Body: The majority of affected requests are returning to expected latency and correctness. We are completing a verification sweep and will share a customer postmortem and evidence bundle within 72 hours. If you observe residual issues, please attach sample request ids.

- Permanent resolution/closure: 
  Title: Incident closed — summary and next steps published
  Body: We consider this incident resolved. A concise postmortem and remediation plan are published (link). We are offering replay verification for customers who request it (link to request form).

2) Customer-facing postmortem executive summary (template)
- Single-paragraph summary (for executives/leadership): 
  On 2026-09-14 between 09:10–10:45 UTC, Redwood experienced partial degradation affecting inference responses for customers using the v2 serving tier in the US. The root cause was an upstream cache invalidation sequence combined with an atypical KV cache eviction policy interaction which resulted in truncated and duplicate token emission for ~0.8% of tokens processed during the window. We applied a routing mitigation, rolled back a rollout, and deployed a hotfix to the cache eviction heuristics; normal service was restored by 10:45 UTC.

- Key impact bullets (customer-friendly): 
  - Impacted features: text generation and structured streaming in v2 for a subset of token lengths.
  - Scope: ~0.8% of requests routed through the affected pool; majority unaffected.
  - Customer action: We will provide a replay/evidence package on request. No data leak or integrity loss detected.

3) Customer action card (decisions and steps)
- Option A — No action needed (default): if you did not observe anomalies, no action required.
- Option B — Request replay verification: we will re-run matching requests against a validated baseline and provide diffs and timestamps. Customers can request via the replay form (internal link). Include tenant id and sample request ids.
- Option C — Roll to safe-model: for customers wanting immediate conservative behavior we can pin to stable model variant (latency cost may increase). Contact your CS owner.
- Option D — Audit & evidence bundle: request the full evidence kit (server traces, KV cache events, sampling of requests). This is for legal/regulated customers; delivery timeline up to 7 business days.

4) Evidence bundle checklist (what customers can expect if they request)
- High-level timeline (UTC timestamps): operator timeline, routing decisions, mitigation timestamps.
- Sample request ids + raw request/response pairs for provided samples.
- Aggregated metrics: token-level error rate, latency percentiles during window compared to baseline.
- Operator actions: changelog of config changes, rollout actions, and hotfix builds.
- Signed operator statement (SLA/credit eligibility) where applicable.

Template text for offering replay/evidence (email/snippet):
  Subject: Replay and evidence offer for incident on 2026-09-14
  Body: Hi <CustomerName>, we noticed you may have been routed through the affected pool during the 09:10–10:45 UTC window. We can run a replay for the requests you provide and share a diff and operator timeline. If you'd like this, please reply with 3 representative request ids and your preferred contact for an evidence handoff.

5) Internal operator rehearsal checklist (to include in post-incident review)
- Confirm incident start/stop timestamps are aligned across logging + routing systems.
- Validate the sample set used for customer replays is anonymized and preserves PII policies.
- Confirm whether dedicated customers pinned to older model variants were affected; document exceptions.
- Check automated rollback triggers: should we enable a stricter failure threshold?
- Decide credit eligibility and whether to proactively offer credits or only on request.
- Future guardrails: cutoff points to avoid KV cache mass-eviction in presence of partial invalidation events.

Notes and unresolved questions (to raise in postmortem):
- Why did the eviction heuristic not throttle earlier? Attach kernel and runtime metrics.
- Was there any correlation with sequence-length distribution spikes from a small set of tenants? (early signals indicate yes).
- Can we make the evidence bundle generation a one-click job for CS with sanitized outputs?

Appendix: short checklist for CS owner preparing a customer email before technical appendix is ready
- What did you see? (one sentence)
- When did it happen? (UTC window)
- Are we asking the customer to do anything? (yes/no)
- How can they request evidence or replay? (link + sample request ids requested)
- Who is the point of contact? (CS owner email + phone)

Draft sample customer email (concise):
  Hi <Name>,

  We wanted to let you know about a brief issue we addressed on 2026-09-14 (09:10–10:45 UTC) that may have affected a small subset of your inference calls routed to v2. We've completed a remediation and can offer a replay/evidence package. Reply with 3 request ids if you'd like us to validate behavior for you.

  Apologies for the disruption — we’ll follow up with a short postmortem and an evidence bundle if requested.

  — <CS owner>

Operational heuristics and quick rules for comms timing: 
- First public update: within 15 minutes if customer-visible impact suspected. 
- Update cadence: every 30 minutes until mitigation applied, then hourly while monitoring. 
- Postmortem to customers: 48–72 hours for executive summary; evidence bundle on request within 7 business days.

Links & refs to include in final postmortem:
- Operator timeline (link to incident channel)
- Engineering root cause analysis (link to confluence RCA)
- Replay request form (internal)

Quick TODO for this draft: 
- Get legal sign-off on evidence bundle contents for regulated customers (Priya).
- Create internal form for one-click sanitized evidence export (SRE/infra ticket).
- Validate sample statuspage snippets with comms (Sofia) and publish to canned-snippets repo.

Open: realistic sample text above; need to test on a non-critical incident rehearsal and capture time-to-first-post metric.

End of playlet.

-- Notes to self (rough):
- Keep the customer-facing postmortem < 200 words; technical appendix separate.
- Avoid excessive engineering jargon in the status updates; customers want impact + choices.
- Consider including "what we're changing" bullet in the closure note to show action.
